If the file behaves differently than expected—like trying to hide itself, encrypting itself, or modifying itself—the antivirus flags it as suspicious. The goal is to catch the malware before it can do any damage.

The key characteristics of a virus include:

• **Self-replication**: Most viruses spread by copying themselves to other files or programs.
• **File modification**: Some viruses change the contents of files, while others delete them entirely.
• **Encryption**: Some viruses encrypt files to prevent access, while others delete the encryption key.
• **Command-and-control**: Some viruses have a command-and-control server that allows the attacker to remotely control the infected machine.

• **File hiding**: The virus hides itself from the operating system by changing file attributes.

These mechanisms are designed to make it difficult for antivirus software to detect and remove the virus.
